section: Quantization, Weight Decomposition, and Allocation Tradeoffs
text: LoftQ resolves this by joint optimization: It alternatively applies quantization and low-rank approximation to approximate original pre-trained weights. Alternating singular value decomposition (SVD) aligns adapters with quantization residuals, mitigating low-bit degradation.

section: Quantization, Weight Decomposition, and Allocation Tradeoffs
text: Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation (DoRA) bridges the performance gap to full fine-tuning: DoRA decomposes the pre-trained weight into two components, magnitude and direction, for fine-tuning, specifically employing LoRA for directional updates to efficiently minimize the number of trainable parameters. To eliminate directional gradient graph overhead: The results indicate that the modification leads to a training memory reduction of approximately 24.4% in fine-tuning LLaMA and 12.4% in VL-BART.

section: Proposed Experimental Protocol: Single-GPU Adaptation Benchmark
text: Experimental Conditions. We compare six conditions (r=16): (1) LoRA-16; (2) QLoRA-4 (4-bit NF4, double quantization, BF16 compute); (3) LoftQ-4 (5 SVD steps); (4) DoRA-16 (detached norm); (5) QDoRA-4 (4-bit NF4 with detached DoRA); and (6) AdaLoRA-16 (r init=24, average target r=16).

section: Proposed Experimental Protocol: Single-GPU Adaptation Benchmark
text: Fixed Profiling Constraints. All conditions fine-tune on Alpaca for 3 epochs: sequence length L=2048 via fixed padding and truncation (preventing activation variance), micro-batch b=2, and gradient accumulation factor 8 (effective batch size 16).

section: Proposed Experimental Protocol: Single-GPU Adaptation Benchmark
text: We use AdamW with cosine decay, peak rate 2 × 10-4, 3% warmup, and activation checkpointing.

section: Proposed Experimental Protocol: Single-GPU Adaptation Benchmark
text: To bypass startup transients, 20 warmup steps precede telemetry logging.

section: Proposed Experimental Protocol: Single-GPU Adaptation Benchmark
text: Step-by-Step Memory Tracking Protocol. Telemetry logs memory over 50 steps: (1) Flush cache and reset peak stats via torch.cuda; (2) Record static footprint M static post-instantiation; (3) Log peak allocation M peak = max () post-forward and post-backward; (4) Compute dynamic overhead M dyn = M peak - M static - M opt; (5) Log reserved memory M reserved = max () to monitor fragmentation; and (6) Measure tokens/second via CUDA timers alongside 5-shot MMLU and 8-shot GSM8K accuracy.

text: Hu et al. identify a major deployment constraint when serving multiple concurrent tasks: For example, it is not straightforward to batch inputs to different tasks with different A and B in a single forward pass, if one chooses to absorb A and B into W to eliminate additional inference latency. Furthermore: Whether 2-bit quantization paired with low-rank adaptation can maintain complex reasoning fidelity across arbitrary model architectures without task-specific calibration remains unverified across general deployment settings.
